name: Paycocke's House

dates.built: C15 and C16; the main range c.1505
dates.altered: Altered c.1600 -- when the main range was reduced from three storeys to two -- and in the C18; restored 1910, the close-studded main elevation 'comprehensively restored' with carving by Ernest Beckwith.
dates.note: Historic England 1337597 dates the main range c.1505; the node's exemplar year is 1509. Both are recorded and neither is changed.

refs.title: Paycocke's, Coggeshall - 1337597
refs.note: Grade I. 'Date first listed: 02-May-1953'; 'Date of most recent amendment: 06-Sept-1988'. The list entry name is 'Paycocke's' and the statutory address 'PAYCOCKE'S, 25, WEST STREET'; the node's exemplar calls it Paycocke's House, which is this record's `name` because the exemplar is the join key.

survey.prepared: Date first listed: 02-May-1953; Date of most recent amendment: 06-Sept-1988, as the Official list entry block prints them. The Details section opens with the legacy header 'TL 8422-8522 COGGESHALL WEST STREET (south side) 9/227 No. 25 (Paycocke's) 2.5.53 (formerly listed as Paycocks House) GV I'.

quotes.text: House. C15 and C16, altered c.1600 and in C18, restored 1910. Timber framed, plastered with some exposed framing and brick nogging, roofed with handmade red plain tiles.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, opening paragraph

quotes.text: Main range of 5 bays facing N, c.1505, with C19 axial stack near right end and 2 rear stacks, late C16 and C18. 3-bay wing to rear of right end, C15/early C16, with stack in rear bay. Beyond it, and originally separate, is a 2-bay building jettied to the left, C15, with a short connecting link.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, opening paragraph, following the materials sentence

quotes.text: 2 storeys (the main range reduced from an original build of 3 storeys c.1600).
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, following the description of the rear wings

quotes.text: Ground floor, 2 square oriels and 3 fixed lights, and 5 similar oriels on first floor, all C20, in early C16 style.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, north elevation description

quotes.text: In the main range all the rear posts continue upwards above the girt which now effectively forms the rear eaves plate, sawn off when the building was reduced from 3 storeys. There are structural indications that the left bay was added shortly after the original build. Close studding with curved bracing trenched into it is exposed in most rooms.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, interior description

measurements.note: AS STANDING. The same sentence says the main range was reduced from three storeys about 1600, and the interior description says the rear posts were 'sawn off' then -- so a two-storey reading of this building as built is wrong.

note: Tranche 3, English medieval fabric and the Tudor house, 5 Sep 2026. Extracted twice with different queries; the second returned the Official list entry header the first had not. THE MOST USEFUL THING THE ENTRY SAYS IS A DEMOLITION: a five-bay merchant's house of about 1505 built three storeys high and cut down to two about 1600, with the sawn-off posts still readable inside. The node's own note describes only the display framing on the front.
